reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes oxide glaze formation and wear reduction in different material systems (NiX and FG samples), not in CoCrFeNi. No evidence is provided that severe plastic deformation of CoCrFeNi yields the claimed nanohierarchical microstructure, nor that such a microstructure promotes glaze formation in this alloy. The key premises about the specific alloy, processing, and quantitative predictions are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Severe plastic deformation of CoCrFeNi creates a nanohierarchical microstructure with high grain-boundary density.
High grain-boundary density promotes rapid, uniform oxide glaze formation during sliding.
The oxide glaze layer reduces friction and wear by mitigating adhesive and oxidative wear.
This mechanism is effective from room temperature to 800 °C.
The nanostructured alloy will show ~25% lower friction and significantly lower wear than coarse-grained CoCrFeNi.
